status: One unchanged whole-claim reuse with a prepared local-community protocol; source-fit authoring, not certification of every pupil’s community or actual attainment.

prior-territory-programme.role: Retain the complete own-school and second-place resource protocol and all traditional/treaty/reserve distinctions, not only a name-recognition component.

mcfntreaty13.role: Previously verified Nation account places Etobicoke within Toronto Purchase Treaty 13 lands; no exclusive parcel/title inference.

gct3.role: Previously verified Treaty 3 territorial/relationship reference; map and source attribution retained.

kenora.role: Previously reviewed City account attributes Kenora’s traditional territory to Anishinaabe of Treaty 3 and Métis people; not a one-people-exclusive-city rule.

preparation: An adult verifies the actual named community and a public/locally verified place within it against appropriate Indigenous Nation/community, treaty and local institution references. School-region worked examples are source models, not automatic certification of a different whole community.

Prepare an attributed local packet showing the supported territory/territories, applicable treaty reference or explicit no-established-treaty finding, source/date, broad location and limits. Record multiple supported peoples/accounts or disagreement. No pupil’s home address or identity is needed.
Retain the existing two actual regional worked cases and whole school-resource operation for the shared claim. A current reserve, municipal boundary or classroom atlas alone is not sufficient.
learnerActions: Identify the traditional territory or territories and applicable treaty reference supported for the actual own community, explain which sources support the answer and distinguish those references from a present reserve.

Explain where the relevant information was found and why a general political atlas may omit it. Explain why knowing the attributed historical/current relationships matters without requiring an acknowledgement performance or deciding a legal title dispute.

Use the second verified regional packet for transfer; explain why the first place’s names/treaty and the nearest reserve cannot simply be carried over. Keep current mapped boundaries and historic/source accounts distinct.
own-community.success: Actual own-community territorial/treaty identification with source attribution, the complete territorial-reference distinction and second-case transfer; not generic Indigenous recognition or copied place names.
own-community.parameterizedCondition: The authoring design requires an appropriate actual local packet. If its sources are missing/conflicting, that application remains unverified until the adult resolves the resource condition; another community’s worked example does not certify it.

ageContextBoundary: Add only 11–12 Ontario context. Preserve the complete existing 6–7 interval and its standards; the derived envelope’s endpoints do not certify ages in the intervening gap. No old age floor is lowered.
claimBoundary: Reuse the unchanged entire Traditional and treaty territories in Canada claim and original guide. The community-specific task does not expand a mastery claim or transfer prior learner estimates.
